newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn prices stable as more imports seen.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn prices stable as more imports seen.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were generally stable this week amid ample stocks despite drought in a number of growing areas, traders said on Tuesday.

"There has been a prediction that the harvest will be a failure in Lampung province next month because of the unfavourable weather. But we believe there will be no problems with harvest in Java despite the (seasonal) drought," said one trader.
Traders' demand for corn in the local market was stable, but many players still stayed sidelined to wait for fresh leads.
One trader said three Panamax ships carrying at least 100,000 tonnes of U.S. corn would arrive in early August.

"Generally, both buyers and traders are still sidelined and are waiting for further developments before taking positions," he said. "Stocks in Java, for instance, are still ample and demand remains good," he added.
Some parts of densely-populated Java island have been experiencing severe drought conditions, but experts have said the weather was seasonal and not related to the El Nino factor.
Traders said corn was quoted at 395-97 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 380-385 rupiah/kg in Jakarta a week ago. Soymeal was quoted unchanged at 885-890 rupiah.
